raw:
The 4+ deck is done and committed on feature/US-01-03, three commits on top of main, not pushed. Gates are green, and the final acceptance run on the head commit 11fc819, with a clean tree, passed everything.

Local run evidence: Jest wrote 91 unit tests to junit/unit.xml with 0 failures. That includes 38 AC-01-03 cases in six suites (AC-01-03-1 to AC-01-03-6). The release APK checks in junit/release.xml also had 0 failures; one of them (AC-01-02-7 step 2) confirms the 4+ texts are embedded in the release bundle. The Maestro flows passed.

run.json shows the six AC-01-03 tests as `skipped`. That is because collect_run.py reads only Playwright and Maestro output, not Jest JUnit — the same thing happened in the US-01-02 runs. The real evidence for them is the CI JUnit report, matched by id in the test names. I started the local API 32 emulator (AVD Medium_Phone) myself for the run and stopped it afterwards.

- **Reused code:** I moved the deck checks from the 3+ tests into two shared helpers that every deck story calls: `tests/unit/deck-criteria.ts` and `tests/unit/age-suitability-record.js`. The AC-01-02 test files now call them with the 3+ settings. I compared the AC-01-02 test names before and after (38 each) and they are identical, so CI still matches the 3+ tests by id.
- **Independent review:** a reviewer subagent attacked all 50 questions in both languages for second correct answers and found none. It flagged four wordings: 4p-22, 4p-29 ("gawra" is too hard for a 4-year-old), 4p-38 (the English was ambiguous) and 4p-40. I reworded all four, and also 4p-47, and added the near misses it checked to the record.
- **Content:** the deck has 12 educational, 12 popular-science, 14 nature and 12 trivia questions. None asks for an answer that a 3+ question asks for.
